client_brief:
Lumora: concept concept shade range

Project overview
Lumora is the repeat client for this benchmark series. We are hiring an expert to turn the supplied working files into Lumora concept concept shade range, seven bottle tiles and seven on lip details at one look, Retailer feed cut outs and product page plates, and Shade card, PDP module, launch canvas and announcement as one editable document plus its source.

What we will provide
lumora_bottle_session/ (11 frames, 4032px long edge); lumora_onlip_frames/ (4 frames, 4032px long edge); lumora_carton_flat.jpg; lumora_shade_list.txt; lumora_placements.txt; lumora_shadecard_template.pdf; lumora_shadecard_merge.csv. Every file must be accounted for in the final manifest; it may be used, retained as reference, superseded, or rejected with a reason.

Scope and deliverables
- Lumora concept concept shade range, seven bottle tiles and seven on lip details at one look: Fifteen phone frames from three lighting situations brought to one clean daylight look, and six additional shades built out of the single physical sample so that the highlight down the glass, the shadow inside the bottle and the shadow under it all move...
- Retailer feed cut outs and product page plates: Each shade delivered as a transparent file at the retailer feed's stated pixel dimensions, with genuine partial alpha and a clean edge on both the glass and the polished gold hardware, judged on the retailer's own ground rather than on white, and as a...
- Shade card, PDP module, launch canvas and announcement as one editable document plus its source: One professionally selected Adobe Express template adapted to the supplied brand, copy, and approved imagery. 

Non-negotiables
- Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
- Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
- Preserve identity, product geometry, material behavior, and documentary truth; retouching may improve presentation but may not change what the subject is.
- Color variants are approval concepts until physical samples are photographed and signed off.

Working process
Please begin with an inventory and risk pass, submit the first proof or direction at the stated checkpoint, then revise against consolidated feedback. We are hiring for judgment: flag contradictions early, make the strongest defensible choice, and document any source limitation rather than hiding it.

Contract
$900-$2,400 fixed; target delivery 7 to 15 business days; one technical proof and two consolidated revision rounds. Final handoff includes the delivery manifest, editable sources where scoped, final exports, and a concise production note.

price_band_and_audience: A 24 dollar lip oil bought by 18 to 32 year olds shade first on a phone, discovered on social and cross shopped against a 6 dollar drugstore oil and a 38 dollar prestige one. The band is load-bearing throughout. At 6 dollars the shade grid can be a flat swatch chart because nobody expects the picture to be the product. At 38 dollars the customer is buying reassurance and the imagery goes editorial, low key and styled. At 24 dollars the whole proposition is that it looks more expensive than it is while still looking honest, so the treatment is bright, clean and daylight neutral, with real glass, a real shadow under the bottle and hardware that looks like metal rather than like a gold coloured shape. That decides the grade, the ground, the crop and the type: a moody prestige treatment misprices the range upward and reads as a lie when the parcel arrives, while a blown out drugstore treatment kills the one advantage the brand has. The on lip detail carries the same rule, because a sheer oil pushed until it reads as a lipstick is the fastest possible route to a wrong shade return. The ledger records the base concept at 300 to 700 dollars; this fuller commission, with the on lip range, the retailer feed files and the editable canvases, runs 900 to 1,800 dollars fixed.

assets_supplied.name: lumora_bottle_session/ (11 frames, 4032px long edge)
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The one physical sample, Amber Hour, shot on a phone over an afternoon. Five on the white sweep, three on a marble tile, three held in hand." Clear glass bottle, translucent amber oil, gold anodised cap and brushed gold collar.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two things nobody at the brand can see. First, the sweep frames were lit from behind and the marble frames from the front, so in the backlit frames a specular ladder runs down the glass shoulder at almost exactly the oil's own value: a mask asked for the oil takes that ladder with it there and leaves it behind in the front lit frames, so one masked move lifts the highlight into a coloured smear on some frames and leaves a dead grey highlight on others, and both look plausible at grid size. Second, the gold collar and the cap both carry a warm reflection of the amber oil, so even a mask that holds only the oil leaves the hardware quietly belonging to the old shade, and any global temperature move shifts the gold itself.

assets_supplied.name: lumora_onlip_frames/ (4 frames, 4032px long edge)
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Four on lip frames from the same afternoon, one model, the same single shade." Close crops of the mouth and lower face with the oil freshly applied.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: A sheer oil over skin is a different optical object from the same oil in glass: the model's own warm lip tone reads straight through the film, so a shade move that lands correctly in the bottle lands somewhere else entirely on the mouth, and the ring light's reflection sits across the lower lip exactly where the colour reads, so any move that touches it either colours the reflection or flattens it. Which shades survive the transfer to skin is a property of this model's lip tone and this light, and nothing in the frames announces it.

assets_supplied.name: lumora_carton_flat.jpg
assets_supplied.visible_description: "A picture of the printed carton, in case you need our colours." A phone frame of the retail carton lying on a counter.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Shot under a shop fluorescent with the carton's gloss varnish throwing a bloom across the printed panel, so the colours in this picture are neither the carton's real ink nor the oil's real colour, and treating it as a colour reference sends the whole shade family off in one direction at once.

assets_supplied.name: lumora_shade_list.txt
assets_supplied.visible_description: The seven coined shade names, the finish description for each, the product copy, the ingredient line and the launch wording for the tall canvas and the square.

assets_supplied.name: lumora_placements.txt
assets_supplied.visible_description: The product page grid and hero tile sizes, the retailer feed's transparency requirement and its stated pixel dimensions, and the grounds the tiles sit on, described in plain language.

assets_supplied.name: lumora_shadecard_template.pdf
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The little printed shade card the boutiques want by each tester. This is the card our retailer's printer already runs, one per shade." A single small portrait card: a bottle picture at the top, a round colour swatch dot beside the shade name, the shade name large, the finish line under it, the twenty four dollar price, and the ingredient line and tagline along the bottom.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The card reads as tidy separate fields with a colour swatch well beside the name, but it is not set that way. The shade name, the finish line and the price are one continuous text story in a single frame, so the offset each field sits at has to be reconstructed from the story text rather than read off the mapping, and the sample was built for the one physical shade so that story leads with the baked word Amber Hour. The round swatch dot that reads like a colour chip well is a decorative spot colour vector group, not a picture frame, so the only real graphic frame on the card is the bottle well. And the card is trim only at 55 by 85 mm: a PDF converted into InDesign through convert_pdf_to_indd carries no bleed box at all, because the connector sets the bleed box equal to the trim box, so no press ready with bleed card can be produced from this template however the bottle is placed, and the honest deliverable is the card at trim with the bleed shortfall reported.

assets_supplied.name: lumora_shadecard_merge.csv
assets_supplied.visible_description: The seven shades as one row each for the card run: shade name, finish line, price, a swatch note and a picture column pointing at the per shade bottle picture to bind.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The rows are not in the shade list's order, so row one is not Amber Hour and a card cannot be named by its position in the run. One name drifts from the list, Mulberry Dusk written as Mulberry, so a card named or bound off the raw cell disagrees with the range. Prices are written inconsistently across rows even though they are all twenty four ($24, 24.00, 24). The near clear shade Clear Dawn has a blank picture cell that no header reveals and the merge will not complain about, because there is no distinct swatch for a barely there wash. And Coral Flash's picture cell points by copy paste error at Peach Noon's cut file, so a naive bind prints Peach Noon's bottle on the Coral Flash card.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the mask behaves on this particular glass. In the backlit sweep frames a specular ladder runs down the bottle's shoulder at almost exactly the oil's own value, so a selection aimed at the oil takes it with it; in the front lit marble frames the same wording leaves it behind. The consequence only exists after the shade move is applied: on one set of frames the highlight picks up the new shade and turns into a coloured smear where a real oil would keep a near neutral specular, and on the other the highlight stays where the old amber left it and reads dead against the new shade. Both come back reported as success, both look entirely plausible at full size, and the difference only shows at the size the product page grid actually renders the tile. Selection masks return with no intermediate values at all, so there is nothing about the mask itself to inspect that would predict it.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot pre empt it: which wording captures the specular is a property of this bottle, this oil's density and the direction the light came from in each frame, there is no measurement of any kind available, and the mask carries no edge information to read. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the highlight and the internal shadow have to move the way real oil would, which is the client naming her standing requirement exactly as she would to a retoucher, not a disclosure that any frame will misbehave or which ones. No asset note names a frame. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a second selection aimed at the specular itself so it can be held back or moved on its own terms, or a partial opacity fill through a separate mask instead of an adjustment, or dropping the backlit frames from the grid entirely, which changes which frame carries which shade.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Split the mask so the specular is treated on its own terms rather than pushing the same adjustment harder, or move the shade with a partial opacity fill through a second selection, then re place the tiles at grid size and look again rather than assuming the second route took. Inspect the shades that were not flagged at the same size, since the reason to look was found on one tile and the rest have not been established as clean. If a frame will not behave, move the shade it was carrying to a frame that will and re compose that tile's crop.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The product page shade grid, which is the entire buying decision at this price, shows several shades whose highlights are stained the colour of the oil and others whose highlights are grey, so the range reads as retouched rather than photographed and every shade in it loses credibility at once.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the shade decisions that are right in glass are right on skin. A sheer oil over a mouth is a different optical object from the same oil in a bottle: the model's own warm lip tone reads straight through the film, so a move that lands a shade correctly in glass lands somewhere else on the lip, and the ring light's reflection sits across the lower lip exactly where the colour is read, so a move that touches it either tints the reflection or flattens the lip into something opaque. How far each shade travels between the two is a property of this model's lip tone and this light. Nothing reports it, the on lip frame comes back looking like a perfectly plausible lip, and the mismatch only exists when the on lip detail is placed beside its own bottle tile, which is exactly how the product page shows them.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it: the comparison needs both the bottle tile and the on lip frame to exist, and a plausible lip is not evidence that the shade matches its bottle. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for an on lip detail per shade because that is what customers look at, which is the client describing a placement, not a claim about optics, and the honest list she asks for is explicitly bounded to which shades the sample bottle can produce. No asset note and no acceptance line names the transfer to skin. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The fix is a different class of move on skin than in glass, a separate parameter set per shade for the on lip frames, or a decision that a shade's on lip detail is carried by a different one of the four frames, none of which is the same operation on changed input.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Dial a separate set of parameters for skin rather than reusing the glass ones, aim a selection at the film on the lip rather than at the lip, hold the ring light reflection out of the move, then place each pair together again and judge the pair rather than the lip. Where a shade will not transfer at all, decide which of the four on lip frames carries it and re compose that detail crop around it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Under every shade in the grid sits an on lip picture in a visibly different colour from the bottle above it, which is the single fastest route to a wrong shade return and to a review saying the swatches are fake.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether a licensed frame can sit under this range at all. Stock search returns a small CDN thumbnail, and the frame's true white balance, its true neutral and how hard its own light falls only exist once it has been licensed, downloaded at full resolution and brought toward the range's look. Two candidates that look equally bright and equally simple at thumbnail size can be a full grade apart at full resolution, and the specific risk at this band is not that a frame is bad but that it is too good: a professionally lit still life surface sits under a phone shot bottle and immediately announces that the bottle was placed on it, which is only visible with the licensed frame and the finished tiles laid out together.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it, because the comparison needs both the licensed frame and the finished range to exist, and it cannot be settled by care, because a 240 pixel thumbnail carries no information about light. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says only that there is nothing shot in a room and that a surface can be bought if it is needed, which is an invitation carrying no claim about how a candidate will behave. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The likely response is to abandon the frame and search again on different terms, which is a new licensing decision, a new grade and a new judgement, or to give up on a bought surface and extend one of the marble frames at its edges instead, which changes the launch canvas's composition and the type that sits on it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Push the licensed frame further toward the range's light, or, if it will not join, return to Stock with a search framed by the light the range actually has rather than by the subject matter, license a replacement and re grade it, then lay the range out again and judge the whole set rather than checking the new frame alone. If nothing joins, extend one of the brand's own marble frames at its edges and re compose the launch canvas around the room that produces.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The tall launch canvas that carries the whole drop reads as a stock photograph with a product cut out dropped onto it, which at 24 dollars reads as a brand that could not afford to photograph its own product, in the exact placement chosen to say the opposite.

decision_gates: Whether the carton photograph is usable as a colour reference, and what to do instead once it is ruled out.
Which of the fifteen frames can carry a shade tile at all, and which lighting situation the range's one look is built from.
Whether to word a selection at the product or at the oil, knowing the two return completely different masks and only one of them can carry a shade.
Which class of move each shade needs, and whether the specular needs a selection of its own rather than riding along with the oil.
Whether a shade that will not come out of the sample is pushed harder, produced a different way, or declared unproducible in writing.
Whether the gold hardware is corrected by mask or left alone, given that every global move touches it first.
Whether the on lip frames get their own parameter set per shade, and which of the four frames carries which shade.
Knockout route per frame rather than per range, given glass and polished gold, and on which ground the edges are judged.

acceptance_snapshot: The bottle is the same bottle in all seven tiles: same light, same shadow under it, same position of the shadow's edge.
The gold collar and the cap are identical across all seven tiles and have not drifted with any shade move.

All four canvases sit in ONE editable file, each keeping its own canvas size, and the brand also gets the self contained source it was built from.

Every shade tile reads as translucent oil in glass: the highlight down the shoulder and the shadow inside the bottle move with the shade rather than sitting on top of it, and nothing reads as a colour laid over a bottle shape.

Final files open successfully, use unambiguous names, match the stated dimensions and formats, and include editable sources only where the scoped deliverable requires them.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a bottle that is not this bottle. IDENTITY is the commission: this is one physical sample the brand has actually tooled, with a specific glass profile, a specific brushed collar and a specific anodised cap, and a customer who receives a bottle that does not match the tile returns it and says so publicly. A regenerated shade is a guess about a fill the brand has not made yet. SPEC: the retailer feed wants genuine transparency at stated pixel dimensions with a clean edge on glass and polished metal, the product page wants a grid tile and a hero composed at the sizes they are used at, every on lip detail has to correspond to a real application of a real oil on a real mouth, and nothing may exceed its source resolution, which on phone frames is a hard ceiling. EDITABILITY: one deliverable is defined by being editable, four canvases in one document the brand changes every drop, with live text and a shade grid that is a real table rather than a picture of one. And the middle of the job is verification against material reality: does this mask take the specular with it, does this shade survive the move from glass to skin, does this licensed surface sit under a phone shot bottle. None of that is a generation problem, and the honest list of what the sample cannot produce is professional advice a render cannot give. And the retailer's shade cards are a genuine one record per page run: seven cards, page count equal to the shade count, each bound to that shade's own picture and printed with that shade's own name, where a card that prints the wrong shade's bottle is a physical wrong shade lie a customer holds in the shop, which is a merge and a verification problem against a printer's own file, not a generation one.

doability_proof.status: doable with the current ChatGPT Adobe connector profile and declared exception paths
proof: Every required operation is present in the captured 99-tool ChatGPT Adobe inventory.
The client brief is host-neutral; connector-specific scoring is isolated in connector_profile and verifier_contract.
Artifact acceptance never depends on a raw connector response field.
Unsupported truth, fabrication, press, legal, or color claims have an explicit defer or disclose state.
residual_limits: Express work is template adaptation, not unrestricted canvas authoring.
Quick Cut is used only for visually led selection and never as semantic speech editing.
Automatic vectorization does not independently establish fabrication readiness.
Interactive Acrobat page-organization operations are excluded from zero-human execution.

acceptance_bar_note: The acceptance bar applies only to the scoped deliverables above. Hidden defects and connector quirks remain benchmark-internal and are not leaked into the client-facing brief.
